title: Tilly and Pip's Strawberry Surprise
markdown:
Sunbeams danced on the soft green grass like tiny golden fairies. In a cozy garden of plump purple pansies and tall nodding sunflowers lived Tilly the guinea pig and Maple the teddy bear. Tilly’s fur was dandelion-fluff soft. Her whiskers wiggled whenever she had a clever idea. Maple was a little bit squishy and smelled faintly of warm honey.

Today the whiskers wiggled extra hard.

“Maple,” Tilly squeaked, voice like a tiny tinkling bell. “I’ve had the most perfectly splendid idea.”

Maple blinked his button eyes. “Oh, Tilly? What is it?”

“Pip the mole. He’s always so shy. He peeks from his burrow but he never plays. I think he needs a special treat. A truly happy surprise.”

Maple understood shy. He sometimes felt shy meeting new ladybugs. “What kind of treat makes a shy mole smile?”

“Strawberries,” Tilly declared, quivering. “The biggest, reddest, juiciest from the Sunny Patch. Little drops of sunshine. Pip loves red things. I’m sure of it.”

Maple’s buttons sparkled. “Splendid. But how will we carry them? A cartful sounds heavy.”

Tilly pointed at a fallen wooden spool from Mrs Higgins’s sewing basket, round and sturdy. “We’ll make a cart. You push. I steer.”

Tilly nudged the spool with all her might. Maple pushed from behind with a soft paw so it would not roll away too fast. It wobbled left, then right, then left again. Maple held Tilly’s ear a moment to keep steady. Tilly giggled. With wiggling and giggling they had a cart. They set off toward the Sunny Patch, hearts full of Pip.

The garden made gentle sounds. Leaves whispered. Fuzzy bees buzzed. The spool-cart wobbled over a root and Tilly steered with both paws, tongue out for concentration. Maple hummed a rumbling tune, and Tilly hummed along, wheek-wheek, which meant she was pleased. They passed Pip’s burrow. A nose like a tiny dark button poked out, watched a bright yellow butterfly, then vanished. The butterfly’s wings were little dancing sunbeams. Tilly nearly called hello, then remembered surprises work better if you do not spoil them with chatting.

“Look,” whispered Maple. “Pip likes watching pretty things.”

In the Sunny Patch the strawberries sat like red jewels among bright green leaves, plump and inviting.

“Perfect,” Tilly whispered.

They picked the plumpest. Tilly plucked. Maple placed each berry in the spool with great care, red popping against the wood like cheerful buttons. One berry tried to roll off. Maple caught it with a squishy paw. Tilly imagined Pip’s nose twitching. She pictured a tiny contented sigh.

When the cart brimmed they pulled it back along the path. The sun was warm. The air smelled of honeysuckle and cut grass. Near the burrow they heard a quiet happy chirping, like a tiny bird.

They peeked around a large smooth stone, cool to the touch.

There sat Pip, not hiding. He watched, wide-eyed, a butterfly with wings like painted silk. The butterfly looped and twirled. Pip giggled a soft airy giggle. He was not waiting to be rescued from lonely. He was already in a quiet happy game of his own.

Tilly’s whiskers paused. Maple’s hum stopped.

“Hello, Pip,” Tilly called, gentle as a breeze.

Pip jumped. The butterfly fluttered up into the big blue. Pip looked at his paws. Ears drooped. The giggle went.

Maple nudged the cart closer. Wheels rumbled softly on grass. “We brought you strawberries, Pip.”

Pip looked at the bright red berries, then at Tilly and Maple. A tiny shy smile arrived. He reached, hesitant, and touched a strawberry. Soft. Wonderfully sweet. He nodded, a tiny dip of his head, picked one up, and took a small happy bite. His ears perked. He sighed a contented little sound. Then he pointed to a bright red ladybug crawling on a green leaf, as if to say: I have red things too. You found more.

Tilly and Maple sat beside him. They shared the strawberries, each bite a little sunshine. Pip, braver with friends so close, watched the garden with curious eyes. A new butterfly — or perhaps the same one, forgiven — drifted past the sunflowers. This time nobody jumped. The three of them watched it go.

As sunbeams painted long shadows, the spool-cart sat empty and sticky. The sweet scent lingered like a warm hug. Pip’s burrow still had its dark quiet door. The pansies were still purple. Only now there were three in the grass, and a ladybug, and the last of the red, and that was plenty of surprise.
characters: Tilly (a guinea pig), Maple (a teddy bear), Pip (a mole)
author: StoryGen Community
